items.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: she had these great Fats Waller and James P. Johnson piano rolls. And I used to sit there, I’d pump the piano and watch those notes.

ctx.x: A victrola. And that was my first record player. But I loved Fats, and oh a neighbor who lived right next door, she had a player piano, so I used to go over there, pull out the rolls, and she’d show me how to put them on the piano, and she had these great Fats Waller and James P. Johnson piano rolls. And I used to sit there, I’d pump the piano and watch those notes. I said oh my God, it must be two piano players playing at once, it couldn’t be one. They were great.
And those things were made actually right from — didn’t the fellas play a special piano and they punched those rolls somehow.
